newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps rates Raytheon offering.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps rates Raytheon offering.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co on Thursday assigned a BBB-plus rating to Raytheon Co's $3.0 billion senior debt offering, which was priced earlier today.
Proceeds from the offering will be used for repayment of short-term debt arising from the company's purchase of Texas Instruments' defense business.
The rating assumes the successful integration of Texas Instruments and of Hughes Electronics, which is expected in the fourth quarter of this year.
The rating also recognizes the increased financial leverage and reduced coverage associated with the acquisitions.
Raytheon's funded debt at March 1997 was about $3.9 billion or 45 percent of invested capital.
Pro forma for the two acquistions would increase debt to about $11.5 billion or 54 percent of invested capital.
The debt portion of the Hughes' agreement can vary from $3.9 billion to $4.9 billion, depending on Raytheon's stock price.
Management is focused on reducing debt and returning to the 25-35 percent range, Duff & Phelps said.
